mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising personal consumption expenditures.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (proxied by INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last month indicates a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it signals a potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (proxied by PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in the last month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong job growth.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (proxied by HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates broader economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of high inflation and tight monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% over the last month, it signals strong economic growth coupled with a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% QoQ and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: economic expansion with labor market tightening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong GDP growth and falling unemployment.
